FORD FLOPS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Gangs are targeting Ford cars – breaking an apparent weak locking mechanism to get in and loot the boot of all valuables – we investigate this crime trend.

Unique Selling Point:
- New crime trend
- All over the news
- Confront if we get Ford

Summary:
Every single day, cars are being targeted by criminals gangs – they break the locks and loot the boot of all valuables – but not just any car… Ford is the manufacturer of choice – we investigated why this brand getting hit the hardest. Is it chance or a manufacturing short coming making it a prime target for criminals.


Further information:
BACKGROUND
We interview three different case studies:

Birony - just this week Birony was one of three cars hit at the same shopping centre, on the same day – just meters apart
Sifiso – car broken into a year ago – lost his masters dissertation – shows it’s an ongoing problem
Laura – car broken into at Sandton City on the 1st of April – laptop taken. She saw the CCTV footage – got the number plate – we are able to say the number plate is fake.

This way we are able to show it’s not a new crime trend and that Ford has known about the issue for ages. We are able to show how rife it is. And we are able to show that the criminals are not amateurs using fake number plates.

We speak to VESA – the Motor Vehicle Security Standards Association about the integrity of the locks.

SA Insurance Crime Bureau about the extent of the crime trend and why manufacturers are not responsible.

Hidden Identity – We speak to a former Ford Dealer Priniciple – he’ll explain how often these cases come in and how it’s the client’s issue and nothing is being to address the issue internally.

Script:


STRUCTURE FORD FLOP

VO: South African motorists are constantly prime targets for criminals – be it hijackers, smash & grabbers or just your average car jamming thief. But criminals adapt and evolve using new methods to get to the loot.

LINK: The latest trend is not actually new, it’s not even hi-tech – if anything it’s cleverly taking advantage of an apparent manufacture’s weakness using old school methods to target a specific brand.

BRIONY: Its seems it’s easier to break into the lock than to actually car jam the Ford.

VO: Briony Simon’s 2015 Ford Fiesta, was one of three cars recently hit on the same day at Centurion Mall.

BRIONY: if there were three cars in a row and it was a Ford, a VW and a Toyota – it would be a different story.

VO: With 20 000 rands worth of valuables gone - Briony took to social media and shared a picture on the MY FORD WAS BROKEN INTO SOUTH AFRICA GROUP with thousands of followers. With more than 13000 shares – Briony realised her incident was not random, nor, isolated.

CCTV FOOTAGE

VO: In this CCTV clip you can see just how quickly thieves are able to get into some Ford models – it almost looks effortless, and just like that the crook makes off with the valuables. [SHOT CHANGE]

LINK: There’s no question that Ford is a popular brand with consumers in South Africa. Just here in this small parking lot, there 5 Fords. It’s also a popular brand criminals. 10 min would make for a good paid day.

VO: Inventor Matthew Parker had his Ford Fiesta broken into two years ago, he modified his own lock to prevent it from happening again.

He showed us just how quickly some of the Ford models can be compromised.

MATTHEW: Door’s open. Once that pin is turned – that’s it –
DEVI: What that took you two seconds
MATTHEW: That’s it – takes the criminals as quick – once those pins are turned it’s like a manual override to the car. // that’s the car locked, that’s the car unlocked – that’s the exact same process – when they force the tool in here – it snaps the pins and it turn.

LINK: But experts say it’s a common lock – which is used in many different vehicle brands. But it comes down to how the lock engages with the built in alarm system.

VO: Phillip Bromley is from VESA – the Motor Vehicle Security Association of South Africa - a non-profit organization that regulates the manufacturing and installation standards of vehicle security systems.

PHILLIP: // if you are going to take a barrel lock and you are going to put enough force, it doesn’t matter what brand it is will break. INT1 M9 // The reason that Ford has got a little bit of a problem is that //INT1 M3 they are stealing the contents of the vehicle with the audible alarm being disabled

VO: Bascially, when the door lock is forced open, the alarm doesn’t go off – so the thieves can quietly steal the contents of the car – without drawing any attention.

While this could happen with other vehicle brands as well, Ford appears to be targeted now.

PHILLIP: // the problem that we see here it wasn’t anticipated in the design that this was going to happen

VO: Bromley explained, strictly speaking, this issue affecting some Ford models, is not a manufacturing fault.

PHILLIP: – so it is not malfunctioning, what’s happened there is a weakness // and a modified solution needs to be applied to it. INT1 M24
DEVI: The manufacturer must sort it out – you can’t make it problem – you must fix it, it’s your design flaw, its your car.
PHILLIP: Cant be seen as a design flaw, it’s a security weakness. INT1 M27

VO: But, it’s a security weakness, some Ford owners have been bearing the brunt of for a while now.

In 2017, Sifiso Nkosi’s 2014 Ford Fiesta Titanium was hit in Auckland Park. He stopped briefly on his way to hand in research for his masters degree in educational psychology.

SIFISO: when I came out the lights were flashing and the boot was open and everything gone. //I lost the actual data – so where am I going to get – so it compromised my study // I am still busy with it today – that’s how big a set back it was

VO: Initially Sifiso thought it was just his bad luck – but now realises, he is not at all alone.

SIFISO: // I mean we cannot all of us complain about the same thing, // so clearly there must be something there.

VO: This is a former Ford Dealer Principle – he says the manufacturer has been well aware of the problem.

JAMES: it’s not a new thing that’s suddenly started – it’s been a continuous problem for the last few years.
DEVI: How many cases would you deal with?
JAMES: // the average in a month between 10 to 15
DEVI: is that considered a lot
JAMES: it is a lot
DEVI: This is a gift for criminals
JAMES: Yes, they know this – that is why target Fords

VO: And these criminals are not amateurs according to Bromley.

PHILLIP: //It is not a case that any Joe can do what they are doing, // we are seeing the criminals are actually coming out and they are understanding exactly what to do and how to do it and that it is how they are being able to override it in a very short space of time

VO: 2014 Ford Ecosport owner Laura Clancy has no doubt in her mind that these are professionals at work – her car has been hit twice. Most recently at Sandton City earlier this month. Laura says the CCTV footage she viewed at the centre, was telling.

LAURA: //the way he was so casual about it is what I think actually freaked me out me more. he pulled up in a very nice Audi, silver, sort of a Q something model – he then it looked to me like he had my car keys, he literally pressed something, the lights flash on my car, without looking around, without blinking, opens my boot – takes out my laptop bag, closes it, locks it again and drives off.

VO: We tracked down the owner of the silver Audi from Laura’s break-in using the number plate. It belongs to a Pretoria woman and it seems those plates were cloned.

We spoke to the owner to find out when last she was in Sandton.

UPSOUND MARIANNA clip – 01.20 - Haven’t been to Sandton, definitely not this year.

VO: With no security solutions currently available from Ford, criminal syndicates continue to target cars every single day. And at R4000 to have Ford replace the lock – affected owners are hesitant.

SIFISO: even now I didn’t fix it, it is still like that because I know it is going to happen again, because I went and opened a case and the police told me it happens all the time//.

DEVI: when you fit a new lock is it tamperproof?
JAMES: No, it’s the same lock that gets fitted, the exact same lock that was damaged, a new set gets fitted – it can happen the same afternoon again.

VO: In March 2018 already, Ford South Africa was quoted as saying: its security experts continuously investigate the way cars are targeted – yet to date no modifications have been implemented.

BRIONY: I don’t think it’s sufficient – fix the lock, don’t investigate the problem, there is a problem with crime in South Africa – but that’s not the excuse.

VO: We requested an interview with Ford South Africa, their Spokesperson – Minesh Bhagaloo came back with an unusual suggestion.

UPSOUND CALL MINESH
DEVI: First time in 17 years – send me the questions, I’ll do my own interview….
MINESH:…. I hear you that is the direction the company is taking.

VO: Even Ford owners are confused by the brand’s apparent reluctance to engage on the topic.

SIFISO: // you know that you are not in any wrong or its not your fault it should be easy for you to respond, //, but if you are going to avoid coming out that’s where the problem is because we have to ask ourselves – what are you hiding.

VO: This is from the press statement:

Ford stated that the brand “takes vehicle security very seriously and continuously invests in security measures that are integrated into their vehicles to deter theft.”

For the first time, the manufacturer publically acknowledged that there are: “potential security risks to previous-generations of EcoSport and Fiesta Models” explaining that “the alarm (if fitted) does not sound, when access is gained via the key lock barrel. The immobilization of the vehicle is however still active until the correct key is placed in the ignition of the vehicle.”

This means while the contents of the car can be stolen, the theft of the actual car should not be that simple.

Ford went on to say that they are “testing various options and developed advanced action plans in response” and hope to “finalise and implement solutions in the coming weeks”.

But in the meantime certain Ford Model owners are still at risk and forced to take extra precautions.

LAURA: // instead of going to shopping centre on my way home, I go home now, I put everything away and then I go back to the shops. // it’s not a way to live.

PHILLIP: There are a lot of solutions, some prettier solutions than others. // The fastest reaction you’re going to get is from a VESA fitment centre – they are on the ground – if there is a weakness they will help find a solution.

VO: Although Matthew isn’t a VESA approved fitment centre, he has helped more than 400 people by modifying the lock mechanism in just the last month.

MATTHEW: // the entire long weekend I had about 40 people // there was ford after ford lined up in the parking spaces.
DEVI: Warranty
MATTHEW: //When you bought the car, the salesman didn’t exactly tell you don’t put your stuff in the boot because it could stolen.


PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Every single day, cars are being targeted by criminal gangs. They break the locks and loot the boot of all valuables, but not just any car. Now, some Ford models are the vehicles of choice.

PROMO 2
VO: Some Ford vehicles are being targeted by criminals who break the locks and loot the boot of all valuables – but is it just by chance or a possible manufacturer’s weakness?
PROMO 3
VO: Gangs are targeting some Ford vehicle models, breaking the locking mechanism to get in and loot the boot of all valuables. We investigate this the latest crime spike.

metadata.Summary: Every single day, cars are being targeted by criminals gangs – they break the locks and loot the boot of all valuables – but not just any car… Ford is the manufacturer of choice – we investigated why this brand getting hit the hardest. Is it chance or a manufacturing short coming making it a prime target for criminals.
metadata.Further information: BACKGROUND We interview three different case studies: Birony - just this week Birony was one of three cars hit at the same shopping centre, on the same day – just meters apart Sifiso – car broken into a year ago – lost his masters dissertation – shows it’s an ongoing problem Laura – car broken into at Sandton City on the 1st of April – laptop taken. She saw the CCTV footage – got the number plate – we are able to say the number plate is fake. This way we are able to show it’s not a new crime trend and that Ford has known about the issue for ages. We are able to show how rife it is. And we are able to show that the criminals are not amateurs using fake number plates. We speak to VESA – the Motor Vehicle Security Standards Association about the integrity of the locks. SA Insurance Crime Bureau about the extent of the crime trend and why manufacturers are not responsible. Hidden Identity – We speak to a former Ford Dealer Priniciple – he’ll explain how often these cases come in and how it’s the client’s issue and nothing is being to address the issue internally.
